text: Continuous Integration, or CI, is a modern software development practice where developers merge their code changes into a shared repository frequently, often several times a day. The heart of CI is the automated pipeline. Every time code is pushed, the pipeline automatically builds the entire project and runs a comprehensive suite of tests. This process is critical because it catches issues early, before they can grow into complex, costly bugs. Instead of discovering a problem days after it was introduced, developers receive immediate feedback, allowing them to fix it right away. This reduces integration headaches and ensures the codebase remains in a stable, releasable state at all times.
